editorial_candidates.reason: The title prints det(I-Df) as plain text while the statement and proof typeset the determinant notation. Optional title typography only; body rendering is legible.

diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The example gives an explicit disk model of the RP^2 quotient, antipodal identification on the boundary, and three interior poles whose immersion images coincide at 0. A compact schematic can make those domain identifications and the triple image point easier to track alongside the long parametrization.
diagram_candidates.specific_content_to_draw_or_check: Show a disk as a fundamental domain with antipodally paired boundary points, mark the three distinct interior pole points, and indicate that each extends to a distinct projective-plane point mapped to the same target point 0. Keep the map label beta: RP^2 -> R^3 and distinguish the domain poles from the single image point; do not suggest a global normal side.
diagram_candidates.certainty: The underlying claim is explicit in source and proof; a diagram is optional and would need to be a schematic rather than a faithful rendered Boy surface.

diagram_candidates.why_warranted: The theorem identifies the compactified continuation space, its unbroken open dense locus, and the two possible once-broken boundary product types when the index drop is one. A small moduli-space boundary schematic can connect these set-theoretic formulas.
diagram_candidates.specific_content_to_draw_or_check: Draw an unbroken continuation from p to q approaching either a negative-end break p -> a followed by a continuation a -> q, or a continuation p -> b followed by a positive-end break b -> q; label ind(a)=ind(q), ind(b)=ind(p), the fixed middle window, and the one neck coordinate tending to zero at the boundary. Preserve the two distinct end-break types and avoid implying other boundary strata at index drop one.
diagram_candidates.certainty: The listed boundary forms and index equalities are stated explicitly; the schematic is optional and should follow the local one-neck chart convention of the cited supplier.
